hero_image_alt: Classic and modern cars outside a flint workshop in a Norfolk countryside scene.

faqs: Are car meets in Sheringham free?
Most of our breakfast meets are free to attend; we ask you to RSVP so we can plan parking. Tours, garage nights and race nights are ticketed, and the price is on each event.
Do I need a special car to come along?
No. Classics, modern performance cars, track cars and daily drivers are all welcome, and so are people who come without a car to look around.
Where do I park?
Each event page explains where display cars and visitors should park. Arrive within the arrival window and follow the marshals.
Are meets family-friendly?
Yes. Our morning meets are relaxed and suitable for all ages. Please keep children close around moving cars.
How do I hear about new meets near Sheringham?
Join the newsletter or the Cars and Coffee club and follow the Norfolk hub. New dates are posted there first.
How do I find a good garage or detailer in Sheringham?
Use the local services on this page. Every business in our directory is checked by our team, and members share their own recommendations in the Norfolk hub in the club.
Can my Sheringham business be listed here?
Yes. If you run a garage, detailer, restorer, wrap shop, parts supplier or other car business in or near Sheringham, list it in the directory and it will appear on this page.
Can I sell car parts or products from Sheringham?
Yes. Partner shops can sell through the Cars and Coffee UK shop with their own shop page. See Sell on Cars and Coffee UK for details.
content.label: Sheringham car hub
scene: Sheringham is a traditional seaside town on the North Norfolk coast, framed by wooded hills and the cliffs either side of the promenade.
It sits on the A149 coast road, and the North Norfolk Railway's steam trains run from here to Holt, so classic machinery is part of the town's character.
It's an easy base for drives west to Blakeney and Wells, inland to Holt, or east along the coast to Cromer.

drives.title: West to Blakeney and Wells
drives.text: Blakeney, Morston and Wells-next-the-Sea on the A149.

drives.title: Holt and the heath
drives.text: Over Kelling Heath to Holt, then back on quiet lanes.

drives.title: Cromer and the east coast
drives.text: Through Cromer to Overstrand and Mundesley.

getting_there.car: The A149 runs along the coast through Sheringham to Cromer in one direction and Blakeney and Wells in the other. The A148 and B-roads link it inland to Holt and Norwich.
getting_there.no_car: Sheringham is the end of the Bittern Line from Norwich, and the North Norfolk Railway runs heritage trains to Holt. Event pages show the nearest stop and station, and members often share lifts in the club.

scene: Holt is a Georgian market town a few miles inland from the North Norfolk coast, with independent shops and handsome brick and flint streets.
Quiet lanes, open heathland and the coast road are all close by, so it's a popular stop on weekend drives.
From Holt you can head down to the coast at Blakeney or Sheringham, or across country to Fakenham and Aylsham.

drives.title: Down to the coast
drives.text: Through Letheringsett to Blakeney, then along the A149 to Wells.

drives.title: Heath and coast loop
drives.text: Kelling Heath, Weybourne and Sheringham, back via the A148.

drives.title: Across to Fakenham
drives.text: West on the A148 to Fakenham, back through the villages.

getting_there.car: Holt sits on the A148 between Cromer and Fakenham, with B-roads north to the coast and south towards Norwich.
getting_there.no_car: Holt has no mainline station, but the North Norfolk Railway runs heritage trains to Sheringham, where the Bittern Line goes to Norwich. Buses link Holt with the coast and Norwich, and members often share lifts in the club.

Whether you need an MOT and a service, a detailer before a show, a wrap or new graphics, or a specialist for a restoration project, start with the checked businesses on this page. Every listing in our business directory is checked by our team, and members share their own recommendations in the Norfolk hub in the club.

hero_image_alt: Classic and modern cars outside a flint workshop in a Norfolk countryside scene.

faqs: Are car meets in Fakenham free?
Most of our breakfast meets are free to attend; we ask you to RSVP so we can plan parking. Tours, garage nights and race nights are ticketed, and the price is on each event.
Do I need a special car to come along?
No. Classics, modern performance cars, track cars and daily drivers are all welcome, and so are people who come without a car to look around.
Where do I park?
Each event page explains where display cars and visitors should park. Arrive within the arrival window and follow the marshals.
Are meets family-friendly?
Yes. Our morning meets are relaxed and suitable for all ages. Please keep children close around moving cars.
How do I hear about new meets near Fakenham?
Join the newsletter or the Cars and Coffee club and follow the Norfolk hub. New dates are posted there first.
How do I find a good garage or detailer in Fakenham?
Use the local services on this page. Every business in our directory is checked by our team, and members share their own recommendations in the Norfolk hub in the club.
Can my Fakenham business be listed here?
Yes. If you run a garage, detailer, restorer, wrap shop, parts supplier or other car business in or near Fakenham, list it in the directory and it will appear on this page.
Can I sell car parts or products from Fakenham?
Yes. Partner shops can sell through the Cars and Coffee UK shop with their own shop page. See Sell on Cars and Coffee UK for details.
content.label: Fakenham car hub
scene: Fakenham is a market town in the heart of North Norfolk, on the River Wensum, known for its weekly market and racecourse.
It's a handy crossroads for drives, with the coast, the Holkham estate and quiet country lanes all within easy reach.
Wells-next-the-Sea is about ten miles north, and Holt and Dereham are both a short drive away.

drives.title: Up to Wells and Holkham
drives.text: North to Wells-next-the-Sea, then west along the coast to Burnham Market.

drives.title: Holt and back
drives.text: East on the A148 to Holt, back through the villages.

drives.title: Wensum valley
drives.text: South along the valley towards Dereham.

getting_there.car: Fakenham sits on the A148 between King's Lynn and Cromer, and the A1065 runs south to Swaffham.
getting_there.no_car: Fakenham has no railway station; buses connect it with Norwich, King's Lynn and the coast. Event pages show the nearest stop, and members often share lifts in the club.

scene: Swaffham is a Georgian market town in Breckland, on the edge of the forests and heaths of the Brecks.
Its wide market place and the long forest roads nearby make it a natural meeting point for drives across West and Mid Norfolk.
Thetford Forest is to the south, King's Lynn to the west and Dereham to the east.

drives.title: Into the Brecks
drives.text: South on the A1065 through the forest towards Brandon.

drives.title: North to the coast
drives.text: Up through Fakenham to Wells-next-the-Sea.

drives.title: Mid Norfolk lanes
drives.text: East to Dereham and back through the villages.

getting_there.car: The A47 runs past Swaffham between King's Lynn and Norwich, and the A1065 crosses it heading north to Fakenham and south to Brandon.
getting_there.no_car: Swaffham has no railway station; buses run to King's Lynn, Dereham and Norwich. Event pages show the nearest stop, and members often share lifts in the club.

scene: Hunstanton is a Victorian seaside resort in West Norfolk, famous for its striped cliffs and sunsets over The Wash.
It's the western end of the A149 coast road, one of the region's favourite drives, with Royal Sandringham and the Burnhams close by.
King's Lynn is a short drive south, and the coast road heads east through the Burnhams to Wells.

drives.title: The coast road east
drives.text: Through Thornham and the Burnhams to Wells-next-the-Sea.

drives.title: Sandringham loop
drives.text: South past Sandringham to King's Lynn, back up the A149.

drives.title: Lavender and lanes
drives.text: Inland through Heacham and Snettisham's villages.

getting_there.car: The A149 links Hunstanton with King's Lynn to the south and the North Norfolk coast to the east.
getting_there.no_car: Hunstanton has no railway station; the Coasthopper and other buses run to King's Lynn and along the coast. Event pages show the nearest stop, and members often share lifts in the club.

scene: Aylsham is a small market town north of Norwich, beside the River Bure and the Blickling estate.
It's surrounded by quiet country lanes, making it a relaxed starting point for drives to the coast or into the Broads.
Cromer is about 12 miles north, and the Bure Valley Railway runs from here to Wroxham.

drives.title: Blickling and the lanes
drives.text: Past Blickling to Itteringham, then Saxthorpe and back.

drives.title: North to the coast
drives.text: Up the A140 to Cromer, then west to Sheringham.

drives.title: Down to the Broads
drives.text: East to Coltishall and Wroxham.

getting_there.car: The A140 between Norwich and Cromer bypasses Aylsham, with B-roads west to Holt and Reepham and east to North Walsham.
getting_there.no_car: Aylsham has no mainline station, but the Bure Valley Railway runs heritage trains to Wroxham on the Bittern Line. Buses run to Norwich and Cromer, and members often share lifts in the club.
